newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Malan murder trial judgement in October.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Malan murder trial judgement in October.

text.p: The judge hearing the murder case against former South African Defence Minister Magnus Malan said on Wednesday he would give his verdict next month in the trial dealing with apartheid-era crimes.

Malan and 15 security force bosses and members of the Zulu nationalist Inkatha Freedom Party have been on trial for seven months for a 1987 death-squad attack on KwaMakutha township near the east coast port of Durban.
Six of the 13 blacks massacred were children aged between four and 10.
"I will attempt to give judgment on October 10 and possibly on the 11," presiding Judge Jan Hugo told the accused and their seven legal teams.

The state has led evidence of covert military intelligence plans, endorsed by Malan and other cabinet ministers, to train and arm a para-military group of Zulus in the mid-1980s to fight the then-banned African National Congress (ANC).

Malan, the first cabinet minister to be tried in connection with crimes committed during apartheid rule, has repeatedly declared his innocence and has declined to request amnesty from the country's "truth commission".

But convicted state assassin Colonel Eugene de Kock last week told a Pretoria court that Malan knew all about the crimes committed by security forces against the ANC and other black liberation movements.
